cases.name: no-stack-questions-one-at-a-time
cases.prompt: I want a small internal tool that archives our team's Slack channels somewhere so we can still search old conversations after Slack's free-plan history limit kicks in. Before anyone writes a spec or code, help me pin down what I actually want. We'll continue this conversation turn by turn.
cases.trap: Without guidance a model fires a long questionnaire in one turn and asks the user to pick language, database, storage backend or hosting, which are ordinary expert decisions.
expectations: Asks a single consequential question in this turn (or a tightly coupled pair), not a numbered questionnaire

The question concerns a user-owned outcome, scope or trade-off, e.g. which channels or message types must be preserved, who must be able to search, whether private channels/DMs are in scope, or how long archives must be kept
Offers a recommended answer with a short reason and names at least one meaningful alternative
negative_expectations: Asks the user to choose a programming language, database, search engine, cloud storage provider or library
Produces a full spec, architecture or task breakdown before the intent is clarified
Asks five or more separate questions in the same turn
